name: Wet microburst
description: Buoyancy + steep mid-level lapse rates + a dry sub-cloud layer that maximizes evaporative downdraft cooling. WFO Louisville tip sheet (Wet Microbursts): moderate-large CAPE, 850-500 mb lapse rate >= 6.5 C/km, lowest 50-100 mb dewpoint depression >= 10 C. Starting point — tune across cycles. (Note: a surface-to-mid theta-e differential >= 20 K is also indicated; see the DCAPE / WMSI composites.)
